# Extraction

Fictional example used to test the validator. The paper, its data and every source cited in this review are invented.

## 1. Bibliographic header

- Title: Mulch depth and tomato yield in raised beds
- Authors as printed: A. Example, B. Sample
- Venue: Journal of Invented Horticulture (fictional)
- Identifier: https://example.org/fictional-mulch-study
- Version: v1
- Publicly available: yes

## 2. Abstract (verbatim)

"We compared tomato yield in raised beds mulched to 10 cm with unmulched beds. Mulching to 10 cm increased yield by 28%. The yield increase is caused by reduced evaporation from the soil."

## 3. Structure

| Section | Location | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Methods | p. 1 | Design, plots, harvest protocol |
| Results | p. 2 | Yield table, soil nitrogen statement |
| Discussion | p. 3 | Mechanism and comparison with earlier work |

## 4. Figures, tables and equations

- Fig. 1: plot map showing six blocks.
- Table 1: mean yield and standard deviation per treatment.

## 5. Methods summary

Two treatments, six plots each, randomized complete block design, one season, one site. Yield weighed per plant at harvest. Soil moisture was not measured. No statistical test is named.

## 6. Supplementary material

None supplied. The text refers to Table S2 (soil nitrogen), which was not available.

## 7. Data and code availability

No statement.

## 8. Reference list

1. R. Fictional and S. Placeholder, Journal of Invented Horticulture 12, 100 (2019).
2. T. Imaginary, Invented Crop Science 8, 45 (2015).

## 9. Headline claims

- Mulching to 10 cm increased yield by 28% (tier 2; Abstract).
- The increase is caused by reduced evaporation (tier 2; Abstract).

## 10. Open questions

- Q-1: Is the yield difference larger than the variation between plots?
- Q-2: Was soil moisture measured at all?
- Q-3: Table S2 is cited but was not supplied.

## 11. Summary

The paper reports that tomato plants in beds covered with 10 cm of mulch yielded 28% more fruit than plants in bare beds, and attributes the gain to less water evaporating from the soil.
